system_description.narrative_title: US–Iran stalemate, Iraq exit and Gulf oil disruption
system_description.narrative_summary: A renewed US–Iran confrontation—shaped by the US troop withdrawal from Iraq, competing diplomatic moves (mediators, ceasefire offers, sanctions talks), and hawkish domestic politics—is driving volatility in Middle Eastern oil flows and global energy markets. The system is open: military actions, diplomatic signals, sanctions, financial channels (including crypto), and oil-export infrastructure continuously exchange inputs and outputs with global markets, regional actors, and domestic political calendars, producing feedbacks (price swings, sanctions evasion, export rerouting) that reshape incentives. Mediator efforts and episodic infrastructure recoveries (e.g., Saudi pipeline restarts) intermittently relieve supply shocks, while sanctions actions and funding channels sustain pressure and prolong the stalemate.
system_description.scope: Actors (US, Iran, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, OPEC+, mediators), military presence and withdrawals, diplomatic negotiations and mediator talks, sanctions regime and alternative finance (incl. stablecoins), oil export routes (Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea, pipelines), oil markets and strategic reserves, and near-term political catalysts (US elections, leadership statements).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economic system (international security, energy markets, and finance)
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil markets & OPEC+ production decisions
Regional Gulf security and maritime chokepoints
International financial and sanctions architecture (incl. crypto flows)
US domestic politics and electoral calendar
evidence_headlines: Oil extends gains as Middle East supply concerns persist
US forces exit Iraq after two decades, leaving opening for Iran
Trump denies offering Iran sanctions relief, Tehran says ready for talks
Middle Eastern oil exports rise to highest level since Iran war began
Mediators push to break US-Iran deadlock

variables.name: Foreign military presence level
variables.description: Measures the scale and concentration of deployed foreign military forces in the regional theater at a given time.

variables.name: Troop withdrawal/change rate
variables.description: Measures the tempo of troop drawdowns, redeployments, or force increases over time in the theater.

variables.name: Proxy force activity level
variables.description: Measures the frequency and intensity of kinetic or disruptive operations carried out by non-state aligned proxy groups in the region.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement intensity
variables.description: Measures the overall volume, pace, and depth of official diplomatic negotiations and bilateral/multilateral talks relating to the conflict.

variables.name: Mediator engagement level
variables.description: Measures the degree of third‑party mediation activity, including frequency of shuttle diplomacy and mediation initiatives.

variables.name: Sanctions coercion level
variables.description: Measures the stringency and breadth of economic and financial restrictions imposed as pressure on targeted actors.

variables.name: Sanctions evasion rate
variables.description: Measures the rate at which economic actors adapt to and circumvent restrictions through alternative channels or illicit routes.

variables.name: Alternative finance flow
variables.description: Measures the volume and velocity of value transfers through nontraditional financial channels such as crypto, informal networks, and sanctioned workarounds.

variables.name: Oil export capacity utilization
variables.description: Measures the proportion of export infrastructure capacity (pipelines, terminals, loading berths) that is operational and being used to move crude and fuel.

variables.name: Export route security level
variables.description: Measures the security and freedom of movement along key maritime and overland export corridors against interdiction or attack.

variables.name: Infrastructure repair/restoration rate
variables.description: Measures the speed and throughput of repairs and restorations to damaged or degraded energy-export infrastructure over time.

variables.name: Global oil price level
variables.description: Measures the prevailing market price indicators for crude oil and broadly traded petroleum products expressed as an index or price per barrel.

variables.name: Oil market volatility
variables.description: Measures the magnitude and frequency of short‑term price swings and uncertainty in oil and fuel markets.

variables.name: Strategic reserve volume
variables.description: Measures the total available volume held in strategic petroleum and fuel reserves available for release to markets.

variables.name: Conflict expectation
variables.description: Measures market and stakeholder expectations about the likelihood, scale, and duration of future escalation in the conflict.

variables.name: Political hawkishness
variables.description: Measures the prevailing domestic political tilt toward aggressive or conciliatory policy responses in relevant political audiences.

catalysts.title: OPEC+ meeting to hold output targets
catalysts.description: OPEC+ is set to meet and likely keep production targets steady, influencing near‑term oil supply signaling and markets.
catalysts.rationale: OPEC+ set to keep output targets steady at Sunday meeting (headline).

catalysts.title: Qatari and other mediators intensify shuttle diplomacy
catalysts.description: Third‑party mediators are actively engaging both sides in separate talks to break the US–Iran deadlock.
catalysts.rationale: Mediators push to break US‑Iran deadlock; Qatar mediators press peace deal (headlines).

catalysts.title: US sanctions waiver for Iran‑Iraq flights
catalysts.description: A U.S. waiver for flights between Iran and Najaf is expected, easing specific sanctions related to civilian travel and logistics.
catalysts.rationale: Exclusive: US to grant sanctions waiver for flights between Iran and Iraq's Najaf.

catalysts.title: US feedback on Iran seven‑day trust plan
catalysts.description: U.S. feedback on Iran's short trust‑building plan could trigger limited reciprocal steps or further bargaining.
catalysts.rationale: Iran receives US feedback on seven‑day trust‑building plan (headline).

catalysts.title: Risk of renewed US bombing after midterms
catalysts.description: Statements from U.S. leadership rejecting ceasefire signal possibility of renewed kinetic campaign or escalation after domestic political inflection.
catalysts.rationale: Trump rejects Iran ceasefire, expects renewed bombing after midterms; Trump says US will win Iran war (headlines).

catalysts.title: Debate/decisions on releasing oil stocks
catalysts.description: EU and others are discussing potential releases from strategic oil stocks to blunt price spikes; U.S. reserve levels are already very low.
catalysts.rationale: EU discusses oil stocks release; U.S. SPR at lowest since 1982 (headlines).

catalysts.title: Continued restoration of Gulf export capacity
catalysts.description: Pipeline restarts and resumed Red Sea loading point to ongoing restoration of Gulf export throughput and capacity utilization.
catalysts.rationale: Saudi resumes Yanbu loading; Red Sea oil exports resume; Gulf crude exports rebound (headlines).

catalysts.title: Ongoing US sanctions and designations
catalysts.description: The U.S. continues rounds of sanctions targeting Iran's procurement networks, sustaining pressure and prompting evasion adaptations.
catalysts.rationale: US sanctions 10/13 tied to Iran weapons procurement; ongoing designation headlines.

catalysts.title: Regulatory/enforcement follow‑ups to Tether report
catalysts.description: Senate findings about Tether's role in Iran funding may trigger enforcement or regulatory actions that affect crypto channels used to evade sanctions.
catalysts.rationale: Senate report: Tether USDT aids Iran funding; investigation headlines.

catalysts.title: Banks and analysts lift oil price forecasts
catalysts.description: Major banks and survey analysts have raised 2026 oil forecasts on prolonged Gulf disruption, shaping market price expectations.
catalysts.rationale: Analysts raise 2026 oil forecasts; major banks lift oil‑price forecast (headlines).
